title: Reformers do not deny all honor to Saints; greater excellence deserves greater honor
source_text: X. Quod spectat autem Theologos Ecclesiae Reformatae, solent illis imputare Scholae Romanae Doctores, quod Sanctis omnem cultum & honorem denegent, & simpliciter doceant Sanctos non esse colendos. Verum ab eo multum absunt, & contrarium omnes unanimiter profitentur. Concedunt enim non tantum divinae, sed etiam creatae excellentiae cultum & honorem suum deberi: atque etiam quo major est excellentia gratiae & gloriae quam Sanctis Deus communicat omni civili dignitate, omnibusque naturae donis & privilegiis, eo etiam majori honore & observantia colendam illam & prosequendam esse.
pass_a_gloss: But as for the theologians of the Reformed Church, the doctors of the Roman School usually charge them with denying the Saints every cult and honor, and with teaching simply that the Saints are not to be cultivated. In fact they are far from that, and all unanimously profess the contrary. For they grant that not only divine excellence but also created excellence is owed its own cult and honor: and also that the greater the excellence of grace and glory which God communicates to the Saints is than every civil dignity and all the gifts and privileges of nature, the greater the honor and observance with which that excellence is to be cultivated and pursued.
pass_b_english: Rome often says the Reformed refuse the Saints every kind of honor.
Le Blanc answers that they unanimously say the opposite.
Created excellence, as well as divine excellence, is owed its own honor.
Grace and glory outrank civil rank and natural gifts, and the honor should rise with them.

lemmas.gloss: that they deny every cult and honor

choices.why: The Reformed consent is the point of the thesis, against the Roman charge.
